cor.heading: Cost of Revenue
cor.text:
The Corporation’s cost of revenues was $7,592,982 for the three-month period ended March 31, 2026, compared to $10,795,101 for the three-month period ended March 31, 2025.

Cost of revenue decreased by $2,479,432 year over year as the Corporation scaled back its mining operations and associated power costs as it continues to build out its AI dedicated infrastructure.

Depreciation and amortization expense decreased by $722,687 year over year as the expense associated with the $3.2 million of assets related to the Corporation’s infrastructure and mining equipment that were put into use during the first half of 2024 was offset by the reduction of expense associated with fully depreciated assets.

opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text:
The Corporation’s operating expenses were $5,136,320 for the three-month period ended March 31, 2026, compared to $2,887,143 in the same period of 2025.

The primary drivers in the current period versus the quarter ended March 31, 2025, were due to:

costs.text:
The Corporation’s operating expenses were $5,136,320 for the three-month period ended March 31, 2026, compared to $2,887,143 in the same period of 2025.

The primary drivers in the current period versus the quarter ended March 31, 2025, were due to:

nonop.text: Other income/expense items of note in the current year include the revaluation of the warrant liabilities which resulted in a gain of $784,833 (as compared to a gain of approximately $2.76 million for the three-months ended March 31, 2025).

net.text: For the three months ended March 31, 2026, the Corporation’s net loss was $4,652,345 compared to net income of $1,633,261 for the three months ended March 31, 2025. Highlights of the quarter include:

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Cash used by operating activities for the quarter year ended March 31, 2026, was $6,397,388 as compared to cash used of $10,105,100 for the quarter ended March 31, 2025. The difference is primarily attributed to the change in digital currency items ($1,252,784 versus -$4,469,226, respectively), change in warrant liability (-$784,833 versus -$2,764,723, respectively) and the increase in amounts owed for working capital items in the current quarter (-$2,051,916 versus -$4,276,284, respectively).

da.text: Depreciation and amortization expense decreased by $722,687 year over year as the expense associated with the $3.2 million of assets related to the Corporation’s infrastructure and mining equipment that were put into use during the first half of 2024 was offset by the reduction of expense associated with fully depreciated assets.

wc.text: As of March 31, 2026, the Corporation had a positive working capital balance of $67,218,751, including digital currencies of $13,561,396. The Corporation commenced earning revenue from digital currency mining in mid-February 2020; however, it has limited operating history, and there can be no assurance that the Corporation’s historical performance will be indicative of its future performance.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
The Corporation recognized revenue from colocation service agreements of $3,026,908 for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (as compared to $5,082,795 as of March 31, 2025). The decline in colocation revenue in Q1 2026 versus Q1 2025 is attributed to the Corporation’s transition to building out AI-driven infrastructure during the quarter in one of its previous hosting locations.

The Corporation also recognized revenue from the sale of energy of $3,716,711 for the three-month period ended March 31, 2026, compared to $3,424,916 for the three-month period ended March 31, 2025. Revenue from this acquisition of a business is recognized each month through the operations of the plant through its available capacity that can be sold, and actual generation of power sold.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text:
Revenue from Bitcoin mining was $184,003 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1,212,291 for the period ended September 30, 2025.

For the three-month period ended September 30, 2026, the Corporation self-mined a total of approximately 2 Bitcoins at an average Bitcoin price of US$71,179 (from Gemini) compared to the three-month period ended September 30, 2025, in which the Corporation mined approximately 10 Bitcoins at an average price of Bitcoin of US$105,320.

The primary reason for the minimal amount in the Corporation’s mining revenues as compared to last year was the continued diversification of the Corporation’s revenue streams by entering into the AI GPU rental space and colocation agreements mentioned above in this MD&A. By entering into these contracts, the Corporation was able to utilize its existing infrastructure and power supply and receive consistent payment for consumption.

Exemplifying this transition, during the quarter ended September 30, 2026, the Corporation recognized revenue per its GPU rental agreement with SubQAI for a total of $2,460,858 (as compared to $0 as of September 30, 2025).

From legacy colocation agreements, the Corporation recognized revenue from colocation services of $2,993,432 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (as compared to $3,904,675 as of September 30, 2025).

Colocation services.text: From legacy colocation agreements, the Corporation recognized revenue from colocation services of $2,993,432 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (as compared to $3,904,675 as of September 30, 2025). The decrease in overall colocation revenue in Q3 2026 versus Q3 2025 is attributed to the Corporation’s transition to building out AI-driven infrastructure during the quarter in one of its previous hosting locations, recognizing revenue of approximately $3,315,379 (as compared to $0 as of September 30, 2025).

GPU rental.text: On April 18, 2026, the Corporation entered into a bare metal GPU rental agreement with SubQ AI, a next generation AI company. The 24-month contract carries an expected total contract value of approximately $19.6 million and became effective May 15, 2026. Under the terms of the agreement, Digi Power X will deliver exclusive, dedicated access to a fleet of the latest generation of NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. These systems will be operated on a bare metal basis through NeoCloudz, Digi Power X’s GPU-as-a-Service platform, at the Corporation’s AI data center. The deployment follows NVIDIA reference architecture, and the facility is engineered to Rated 3 standards, with redundant utility feeds, N+1 UPS, and a CDU and chiller based two loop cooling architecture. The Corporation began recognizing revenues from this agreement during Q2 2026.

intro.text: As used in this Annual Report, the terms “we,” “us,” “our,” the “Corporation,” “Digi Power X Inc.” and “Digi Power” mean Digi Power X Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, unless otherwise indicated. The Corporation is an innovative energy infrastructure company that develops cutting-edge data centers to drive the expansion of sustainable energy assets. With multiple sites, including our state-of-the-art combined cycle and high-capacity substations, we tap into and enhance the energy grid, supporting both industrial clients and broader energy markets. Our mission is to create efficient, reliable and cost-effective energy solutions by maximizing the potential of our power facilities and building advanced infrastructure to meet the demands of high-performance computing, bitcoin mining and other energy-intensive industries.

lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Lease liabilities
lines.why: IFRS 16 puts every lease on the balance sheet like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Cash and equivalents
accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: (iv) On April 23, 2026, the Corporation entered into a Simple Agreement for Future Equity (“SAFE”) with Subquadratic Inc., a Delaware corporation, pursuant to which the Corporation invested $250,000 in exchange for the right to receive shares of Subquadratic’s capital stock upon the occurrence of certain future events, including a qualified equity financing.

DOGE Capital is controlled by Michel Amar, the Corporation’s CEO and a director, and each of Michel Amar and Alec Amar, the Corporation’s President and a director and Michel Amar’s son, has an ownership interest in DOGE Capital.
